newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy evacuates 33 in second Albania evacuation.
newsitem.headline: Italy evacuates 33 in second Albania evacuation.

text.p: Italy said on Saturday it had evacuated 33 Italians and Albanians from the troubled southern Albanian port of Vlore, its second such mission within a week.
A foreign ministry spokesman said the group were rescued by navy helicopters and were being transferred to the southern Italian port of Brindisi.
The ministry said in a statement the operation was carried out in conjunction with the defence ministry and with the consent of the Albanian authorities.

The spokesman said 12 Italians and 21 Albanians -- either relations of the Italians, Albanians who had previously been resident in Italy or who had had helped the Italian community in Vlore -- were airlifted in the operation.

Italy on Monday evacuated 35 people from Vlore and the foreign ministry said only a few Italians, mostly members of religious orders, now remained in southern Albania, where armed rebels have mounted an insurrection.

The West has intensified diplomatic efforts to resolve the rebellion and former Austrian chancellor Franz Vranitzky, who headed a European security mission to Tirana on Saturday, said he had "very extensive" talks with President Sali Berisha.
But Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said in a speech in Venice that the unrest in Albania proved just how badly prepared the European Union was for crises on its doorstep.

"The Albanian crisis is a classic European crisis of the post-Cold War era -- too far from the United States for the U.S. to take an immediate interest, too close to Europe for us to ignore it," he said.
"It is also evidence of inadequate analysis and planning. The European Union must equip itself adequately in this respect and with the means to intervene rapidly, including the use of force."

The foreign ministry said Italy had arranged for food and medicines to be sent to a hospital in Vlore run by Italian nuns who had appealed for supplies saying their hospital had been looted and they had nothing to treat burns and gunshot wounds.

Rebels who hold several southern Albanian towns have spurned Berisha's offer of an amnesty during the suspension of a government offensive to crush the insurrection. They have vowed to stand their ground until Berisha steps down.

Seventy Albanians fleeing unrest crossed to Italy on Friday, including 46 who made the trip in a twin-masted fishing boat and who refused to board a vessel sent to repatriate them from the town of Otranto on Friday night.
They said they were seeking political asylum and were transferred to Lecce for officials to consider their cases.
Italy, just 40 miles (64 km) across the Adriatic from Albania, has stepped up security this week, fearing a flood of immigrants.

Tens of thousands of Albanians made a mass exodus to Italy in rusting freighters in 1991 after 45 years of Stalinist rule crumbled in Europe's poorest country. Thousands more have followed in illegal immigration rackets.
